cohort: 40,764 live-born, singleton preterm infants in a non-breech presentation at birth, born after onset of labor between 1999 and 2010 in Sweden
finding: Infants delivered by vacuum extraction had higher odds of intracranial hemorrhage, extracranial hemorrhage, and brachial plexus injury compared to infants delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Infants delivered by vacuum extraction had higher odds of intracranial hemorrhage, extracranial hemorrhage, and brachial plexus injury compared to infants delivered vaginally, while infants delivered by cesarean section during labor did not have an increased risk of these complications.
